key_insight: PADO-Pauli accelerates classical Pauli propagation for variational quantum circuits by compiling observables and circuits once, then reusing sparse GPU computations across many parameter and data batches.
engineering_relevance: This makes gradient-based training of quantum machine learning and variational quantum algorithms more practical by reducing repeated simulation cost and integrating smoothly with PyTorch autodiff.
method: Compile the circuit and observables into sparse matrices with rotation angles expressed as cosine/sine factors.
Reuse the compiled program for batched evaluations over parameters and data inputs.
Support truncation, noise channels, and zero-filtering; gradients flow via a PyTorch vector-Jacobian product.
evidence_signal: On an NVIDIA A100, the system is reported to run up to 10× faster than cuPauliProp on 4–12 qubits, use up to 3.1× less memory on 16 qubits, and match exact statevector simulation up to 28 qubits.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on truncation, zero-filtering, and problem size, so accuracy and speed may vary for circuits with many surviving Pauli terms or heavier noise/models.
paper_title: PADO-Pauli: A GPU-Accelerated Implementation of Pauli Propagation
